## Summary

[Partial] Cut the metal plate to size and bend sections according to relative angles defined in the plans. [t179]

[Partial] Drill holes directly into the frame rails based on provided dimensions. [t179]

[Partial] Remove the factory lightweight aluminum gas tank skid and install a heavier steel version. [t179]

[Partial] Cut the plate to size using a fine-tooth carbide plywood Skilsaw blade, then glue sections with spoolgun MIG welding. [t179]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Consider 1/4" aluminum for lightweight applications if a brake press is available. [t179]
- Use 7075 aluminum to achieve properties similar to steel. [t179]
- Be prepared for trial and error when drilling without pre-punched templates. [t179]
- Use a local metal shop to cut shapes if you lack bending tools, then drill holes yourself. [t179]
- Factory t-case skids take less abuse than other components. [t179]
- [Partial] Consider an aluminum engine skid paired with the new steel gas tank skid for a balanced approach. [t179]
- Use 1/4" aluminum for medium-duty applications. [t179]
- Print PDFs on regular letter paper and tape them together to create a cut pattern. [t179]
